title: Newton’s root iteration
parts: Subtract the function-to-derivative ratio from the current root estimate to get the next estimate.
example: For f(x)=x²−2 and x₀=1, the next estimate is 1−(−1)/2=1.5.
note: The step requires a nonzero derivative and does not guarantee convergence.
wrong: Subtract the derivative divided by the function.

title: Forward finite difference
parts: The change in f over a step of length h divided by h.
example: For f(x)=x² at x=2 with h=0.1, the difference is (4.41−4)/0.1=4.1.
note: At a fixed nonzero h, this can approximate f′(x).

title: Trapezoidal rule
parts: Approximate signed area with evenly spaced ordinates by giving half weight to both endpoints.
example: For heights 2,4,6 at spacing 1, the estimate is 1×(1+4+3)=8.
note: Each endpoint belongs to one trapezoid, while interior ordinates belong to two.
wrong: Multiply the spacing by the sum with all heights given full weight.

title: Absolute error
parts: The distance between an approximation x̃ and the exact value x.
note: Absolute error has the same units as the original quantity.
wrong: The error divided by the magnitude of the exact value.

title: Minimising argument
parts: The choice x∗ is an input at which f attains its minimum.
example: For f(x)=(x−2)², the minimising input is 2 and the minimum output is 0.
note: Argmin finds an input, while min gives the output value.
wrong: x∗ is the smallest output of f.

title: Gradient descent step
parts: Move from the current point against the gradient with step size η.
example: For f(x)=x², x₀=2 and η=0.1, the next point is 2−0.1×4=1.6.
note: A step that is too large can still increase f.
wrong: Move in the positive gradient direction.

title: Linear inequality constraint
parts: Every component of Ax is no greater than the corresponding component of b.
example: Rows (1,1) and (2,0) with b=(5,6) require x₁+x₂≤5 and 2x₁≤6.
note: There is one inequality per row.
wrong: Only the sums of the components are compared.

title: Residual of a linear system
parts: The residual is the required right-hand side minus the result from the approximate solution.
example: If A=2, b=7 and x̃=3, the residual is 7−6=1.
note: The residual measures a mismatch in the equations.
wrong: The residual is the true solution minus the approximate solution.
